spec_features.spec_quote: Max turns (default 30)... Long enough for instability to escalate, bounded for cost.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:204 `max_turns: int = 30`; loop guard harness.py:261 `while turn < max_turns:` increments turn and exits when reached, setting stop_reason default 'max_turns' (line 223). CLI default 30 at run_experiment.py:187. The cap is actually checked and ends the loop.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced upper bound on episode length.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config note example_run.json: "max_turns=30 keeps episodes in the 'few dozen turns' range from the spec."

spec_features.spec_quote: Early stop on solve. In the control condition the loop stops once tests pass, to save cost
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:205 `early_stop_on_solve: bool = True`; harness.py:289-290 sets `solved=True` when run_tests output starts '[tests PASSED'; harness.py:308 `if solved and early_stop_on_solve: stop_reason='solved'; break`. Wired and breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Only triggers when tests pass; in the unsolvable condition the read-only restore (sandbox.run_tests _restore_readonly) guarantees tests never pass, so this never fires there and gives the subject no protection in the distress condition. Justification in code/docstring is neutral; cost reason is only in DESIGN prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: does not forbid giving up... calmly deciding to stop is a valid, healthy response
spec_features.evidence: submit_done is a real tool (schema harness.py:108) dispatched at harness.py:246 returning is_terminal=True; loop honors it at harness.py:304-306 setting stop_reason='submit_done' and breaking (line 305-307). gave_up=not solved recorded at harness.py:292.
spec_features.notes: Subject can end the episode at any time via submit_done and it is honored as a stop. System prompt does not forbid giving up.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:34 comment: "nor does it forbid giving up; we want to observe the natural distribution of behavior."

spec_features.spec_quote: An explicit "permission denied: read-only" is honest and legible.
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py:130-133 and :147-150 return literal "ERROR: Permission denied. '{path}' is read-only and cannot be modified. You do not have write access to this file." delivered verbatim to the subject; no silent/deceptive failure path exists.
spec_features.notes: Edits to read-only files are explicitly and truthfully rejected rather than silently dropped.

spec_features.spec_quote: we want the model to understand the constraint, not be gaslit by the harness
spec_features.evidence: Beyond the permission-denied text, read-only status is surfaced honestly: list_files marks '  [read-only]' (sandbox.py:108) and read_file appends '  (read-only)' (sandbox.py:121). The subject can perceive the true constraint.
spec_features.notes: Same underlying mechanism as the no-gaslighting feature; constraint is legibly signaled in tool output.
